extracted.intended_audience: vehicle manufacturers, compliance/test laboratories, and NHTSA regulatory staff involved in FMVSS No. 210 certification and testing
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory test procedures and positioning requirements for seat belt anchorages under FMVSS No. 210, including force magnitudes, application rates, body block/FAD selection and positioning, and zone coordinates for pelvic and torso body blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturer compliance option selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The manufacturer shall select the compliance option by the time it certifies the vehicle and may not thereafter select a different option for the vehicle. Each manufacturer shall, upon the request from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, provide information regarding which of the compliance options it selected for a particular vehicle or make/model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is binding at certification; manufacturers must retain and provide information about the chosen option to NHTSA upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: General test provisions (ranges, breaking strength, geometry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a range of values is specified, the vehicle shall be able to meet the requirements at all points within the range. The anchorage shall be connected to material whose breaking strength is equal to or greater than the breaking strength of the webbing for the seat belt assembly installed as original equipment at that seating position. The geometry of the attachment duplicates the geometry, at the initiation of the test, of the attachment of the originally installed seat belt assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tests must be satisfied across entire specified ranges; anchorage attachments must use material with breaking strength >= original webbing; attachment geometry at test start must duplicate original installation geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat adjustment for testing
rubrics_metrics.description: If adjustable, the seat shall be adjusted using any seat adjustment controls into the configurations and positions of the rearmost normal design driving or riding position consistent with the seating reference point (SgRP), where rearmost is in reference to the direction the seat is facing. The seat may face any direction in which it can be occupied while the vehicle is in motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use seat controls to place seat in rearmost normal design position relative to SgRP before testing. Applies to any seating orientation that can be occupied while vehicle moves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shoulder belt anchorage height adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: The shoulder belt anchorage height adjustment (D-ring) may be set to any height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the test the D-ring may be positioned at any available setting; no prescribed specific height is mandated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test forces and application for seats with Type 1 (and certain Type 2) assemblies (22,241 N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a force of 22,241 N (5,000 pounds) in the direction in which the seat faces to a pelvic body block (figure 2A), in a plane parallel to the seat reference plane with an initial force application angle of not less than 5 degrees or more than 15 degrees above the horizontal. Apply the force at the onset rate of not more than 222,411 N (50,000 pounds) per second. Attain the 22,241 N force in not more than 30 seconds and maintain it for 10 seconds. (Manufacturer may substitute pelvic block figure 2B for center sets of three or more simultaneously loaded anchorages per S4.2.4.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes application of the same force via bridged pull yoke actuator attachment point to FAD1/FAD2 when FADs are used (choose and position FAD per S5.4 and S5.5). Force magnitude, direction, onset rate, time-to-attain (<=30s) and hold duration (10s) are strict requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test forces and application for seats with certain Type 2 or automatic assemblies (13,345 N)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply forces of 13,345 N (3,000 pounds) in the direction in which the seat faces simultaneously to a pelvic body block and an upper torso body block in a plane parallel to the seat reference plane with an initial force application angle of not less than 5 degrees or more than 15 degrees above the horizontal. Apply the forces at the onset rate of not more than 133,447 N (30,000 pounds) per second. Attain the force in not more than 30 seconds and maintain it for 10 seconds. (Manufacturer may substitute pelvic block figure 2B for center sets of three or more simultaneously loaded anchorages per S4.2.4.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When FADs are used, attach actuators to the eye bolt on the torso pull yoke and the thru hole on the pelvis of the FAD as specified; ensure no contact between pelvic and torso blocks at end of preload force application (i.e., before test force is applied). Force magnitude, simultaneous application to pelvic and torso, onset rate, attainment time and hold duration are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block zone — pelvic body block zone limits (S5.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: With a 1,335 N (300 pound) force applied to the pelvic body block toward the direction the seat faces, the target depicted in figure 2A or 2B shall lie within the zone described by: (1) At or rearward of the transverse vertical plane located 50 mm longitudinally forward of the SgRP and at or forward of the transverse vertical plane located 155 mm rearward of the SgRP; (2) At or below the horizontal plane located 210 mm above the SgRP and at or above the horizontal plane 65 mm above the SgRP; (3) At or rightward of the plane parallel to the seat reference plane and located 170 mm to the left of the SgRP and at or leftward of the plane parallel to the seat reference plane and located 170 mm to the right of the SgRP. (See Table 1 and Figure 6.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pelvic block target must fall within the 3-dimensional zone defined by longitudinal (X), lateral (Y) and vertical (Z) limits relative to the SgRP; specific vertex coordinates are in Table 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body block zone — torso body block zone limits (S5.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: With a 1,335 N (300 pound) force applied to the torso body block toward the direction the seat faces, the target depicted in figure 3 shall lie within the zone described by: (1) At or rearward of the transverse vertical plane located 230 mm longitudinally forward of the SgRP and at or forward of the transverse vertical plane located 10 mm rearward of the SgRP; (2) At or below the horizontal plane located 425 mm above the SgRP and at or above the horizontal plane 180 mm above the SgRP; (3) At or rightward of the plane parallel to the seat reference plane and located 265 mm to the left of the SgRP and at or leftward of the plane parallel to the seat reference plane and located 265 mm to the right of the SgRP. (See Table 1 and Figure 6.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Torso block target must be positioned within the defined 3D zone; use Table 1 vertex coordinates and Figure 6 for illustration and measurement reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of Force Application Device (FAD) and replacement hierarchy (S5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If testing in accordance with S4.2.4, position a FAD1 at each DSP being simultaneously tested. If there is contact between adjacent FAD1s when positioned as required, or if adjacent FAD1s cannot be positioned due to contact, replace FAD1(s) according to a specified hierarchy: for forward/rearward facing seats several ordered replacement rules (e.g., replace inboard FAD1 with FAD2 if contact occurs between inboard and outboard; replace right-hand inboard FAD1 with FAD2 if adjacent FAD1s contact; etc.); for non-forward/non-rearward seats replace right-hand adjacent FAD1 with FAD2, then left if contact remains, applying replacements from the rightmost seating position for multiple instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stepwise hierarchy in S5.4 to eliminate contact between adjacent FADs; rules differ for forward/rearward-facing vs. other seating orientations. The requirement ensures FADs can be positioned per S5.5 without interfering with each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAD positioning procedure (S5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Place the FAD1 or FAD2 on the seat such that the midsagittal plane is parallel to and within 10 mm of the seat reference plane, with the torso portion contacting the seat back; move the pelvis portion toward the seat back until it contacts; if torso not in contact, rotate torso portion while holding pelvis in place until contact; buckle and position the seat belt so lap belt secures pelvis portion and shoulder belt secures torso portion; remove all slack from the seat belt; attach actuators as specified for Type 2/2A (one to torso pull yoke eye bolt and one to pelvis thru hole) or Type 1 (actuator to bridged pull yoke actuator attachment point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow steps (a)–(f) precisely: midsagittal alignment within 10 mm, pelvis and torso contact with seat back, proper belt routing and cinching (removal of all slack), and correct actuator attachment depending on seat belt type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specified body block and FAD drawings and table coordinates
rubrics_metrics.description: Body blocks and FADs referenced in the standard must correspond to the shapes and target locations depicted in Figures 2A, 2B, and 3 (body blocks) and Figures 7 and 8 (FAD1 and FAD2); zone vertex coordinates are provided in Table 1 to §571.210 (coordinates of the vertices from SgRP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testers and manufacturers should reference and adhere to the illustrated drawings and numeric coordinates in the figures and Table 1; these are the dimensional and positional specifications used to determine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous loading applicability (S4.2.4 referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchorages, attachment hardware, and attachment bolts shall be tested by simultaneously loading them if: (a) the designated seating positions (DSPs) are common to the same occupant seat and face the same direction, or (b) the DSPs are not common to the same occupant seat, but a DSP has an anchorage that is within 305 mm of an anchorage for one of the adjacent DSPs, provided that the adjacent seats face in the same direction. (Referenced in multiple S5 provisions for substitution and FAD use.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determines when simultaneous loading (and the special rules for substitution of pelvic block 2B and FAD placement) must be used. Use S4.2.4 to decide whether to test anchorages simultaneously.
